item.title: MagnaCut’s Inventor Made a New Super Steel That May Usurp the EDC Knife Throne
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 5.47
For the past few years, MagnaCut steel has had a stranglehold on the knifemaking industry. Often referred to as a “super steel,” it is beloved for its unique blend of performance, reliability, durability, strength, corrosion resistance and more. But for 2026, MagnaCut’s inventor has finally launched a potential successor. Called MagnaMax, it had been quietly teased by brands and artisans at shows and conventions before its official unveiling this year. In fact, it’s already available in quite a few knives from some noteworthy brands. What is MagnaMax, exactly? Like its predecessor, MagnaCut, MagnaMax is a CPM (Crucible Particle Metallurgy) steel. This means that, unlike traditional steel crafted from melted-down ingots, it’s created from an atomized powdered spray. This creates a microscopic, even structure that offers generally higher toughness, wear resistance and fewer weak points. Both of these steels were developed by the same person, Dr. Larrin Thomas, a master metallurgist and, understandably, an absolute legend in the knifemaking community.

item.title: Patagonia Reworks Its Modern Mountain Icon into an Everyday Jacket with Mil-Spec Styling
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 5.38
Retro-X. R1. The Houdini. Patagonia’s archive is full of iconic jackets for use on and off the mountain. But when it comes to modern technical performance, the Nano-Air ranks damn near the peak. In Gear Patrol‘s original review back in 2014, we asserted, “The Nano-Air represents the future of protective outwear: a mixed bag of breathability, temperature regulation and comfort.” It was a technical breakthrough in its debut, giving rise to a new category of versatile midlayers for high-output activities, and it continues to set the bar for active insulation more than a decade later. Turns out, it also doubles as a killer urban jacket. Like some of its Patagonia siblings, such as the Nano Puff and Synchilla Snap-T, the Nano-Air has long straddled the divide between mountainwear and urban aesthetics. However, a new entry into Patagonia’s catalog puts the pioneering technology squarely into the latter category.

item.title: Apple Is Quietly Making It Even Easier to Use Your Current AirPods
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 5.10
Most people never dive into their AirPods settings. They simply pop the AirPods in their ears, which automatically pair to their iPhone, and (boom!) they’re listening to music. That’s the beauty of AirPods: It’s easy, and they just work. But for “more advanced” users, Apple provides numerous ways to customize the AirPods experience. A better AirPods experience When paired and in AirPods Settings, you tweak the on-stem controls for switching between listening modes, answering calls and activating Siri. And you can customize these controls for the left and right AirPods. Depending on the model of AirPods you have, you may have access to customize more advanced controls, such as head gestures, sleep detection and using your AirPods as an iPhone camera remote. And that’s really just scratching the surface.

item.title: Casio Transforms Its Iconic F-91W into a Hiking Watch with One Small Change
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 5.03
Casio’s F-91W has been in production since 1989 and remains one of the best-selling watches ever made. Its beauty is found in its simplicity. Housed in a lightweight resin case, the timepiece offers basic water resistance and a host of useful features, all in one of the most GADA-friendly packages you’ll ever find in budget watchmaking. However, there’s always been one hitch in its theoretical perfection: the strap. Since the beginning, the standard F-91W has been paired with a resin strap, which works fine for everyday wear but feels less at home when you’re trekking outdoors. But now, after nearly 40 years of existence, Casio has given the F-91W a trail-ready upgrade. New strap, new personality If you’ve ever wanted to take the F-91W into the backcountry without the plastic strap building up sweat or looking out of place, Casio now has you covered. Introducing the F-91WF, a fabric-strap variant of its most iconic digital watch, giving hikers a more practical alternative to the original resin. Swapping resin for woven fabric sounds minor, but it significantly changes how the F-91WF breathes on the wrist during long days on the trail.

item.title: You’re (Probably) Using Screwdrivers All Wrong
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.97
Since it arrived in the 1930s, the Phillips head has established itself as a staple bit standard of the fastener world, and for good reason. As an improvement on the basic slotted screw and driver, the crosshair cut allowed for easy centering with much more stable engagement. Though it allowed for more torque, it also had the unintended benefit of “camming out” under too much pressure, thereby preventing damage. If you’ve ever stripped a screw, it might be because of this design bug feature. However, it could actually be because you’re mixing standards altogether. Not long after the Phillips head, the Japanese Industrial Standard (JIS) arrived in the 1950s. Eventually, Phillips worked with GKN Screws and Fasteners to create the Pozidriv standard for its own improved design.

item.title: Unimatic’s New $740 UT1-PD Merges Its Toolwatch and ProDiver Lines for the First Time
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.91
Over the past couple of years, Unimatic has amassed more hype than any other young, independent watch brand through its staggering amount of collaborations. However, the brand remains anchored in its pragmatic, high-performance tool watches with minimalist, mid-century aesthetics. Two primary branches of that core catalog, the Toolwatch and ProDiver collections, come together for the first time in the new Modello Uno UT1-PD. The UT1-PD is a limited edition Unimatic hybrid that combines the Toolwatch internal architecture with the ProDiver case and bezel. It features a brushed 40mm stainless steel case that overlaps both collections. Visually, the dial blends the classic printed triangle-dot-dash hour markers of the ProDiver line with the Toolwatch “ghost ladder” handset and dash minutes track. The 41.5mm coin-edge overhanging bezel looks very similar to that of the Toolwatch. However, the 60-minute track is reversed, counting up rather than down to conform to diving standards. It is also accented with an orange triangle on the pip.

item.title: Barbour’s New Bedale Jacket Restores a Rare Detail from Vintage Examples
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.87
The Barbour Bedale might be the brand’s most recognizable jacket, worn by everyone from the British royal family to that stylish dude at your local coffee shop. But the version hanging on the rack is not the one that necessarily built its reputation as the brand’s definitive style. Decades ago, Barbour traded two of the original’s four flap pockets for slanted hand warmers you see on current production models. A new collaboration between Barbour and Japanese retailer Journal Standard reverses that decision, reviving the four-flap-pocket configuration of the OG Bedale and pairing it with some modern adjustments in terms of fit and finish. The Bedale’s original design Barbour introduced the Bedale as a British equestrian jacket: short enough to clear a saddle, with a two-way zip and enough structure to handle wet weather. Since then, it’s become the template for waxed-cotton field jackets.

item.title: 22 New Watches You Might’ve Missed from Seiko, Casio, Breitling, Audemars Piguet and More
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.75
If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more From afar, the watch industry may seem unhurried. But every passing day brings about new timepieces from brands big, small, new and old. Below, find 22 new releases from the likes of affordable brands like Casio and Seiko, luxury legends such as Breitling and Audemars Piguet, and enthusiast favorites like Unimatic and Christopher Ward. Together, they show an industry that never stops ticking — and, centuries later, can still find the time to surprise you. Best New Gear: This article is part of an ongoing series collecting the most important new watches, gadgets, pocket knives and more. Catch up on other releases. Unimatic Modello Uno UT1-PD Limited Edition – ProDiver Unimatic combines its Toolwatch and ProDiver collections for the first time to offer the ultimate GADA watch. The 40mm ProDiver stainless steel case is equipped with the Toolwatch 360 Protection System, packing 300m water resistance and a Seiko smooth-sweeping quartz movement. It comes on Unimatic’s quick-release TPU pin buckle strap and is limited to 250 pieces. Christopher Ward’s Trident 30×30 limited-edition version of its flagship dive watch features a special wave-textured dial in teal with a matching bezel and rubber strap, along with a red coral seconds hand. The color scheme is a nod to the tropical parrotfish, which plays a key role in maintaining coral reef ecosystems. Proceeds of the watch’s sales will go to the Blue Marine Foundation’s ocean conservation efforts. Timex’s Q Marbella sports watch pays clear tribute to the legendary Gérald Genta with a design heavily inspired by his IWC Ingenieur. In addition to borrowing the Ingenieur’s bolted-on round bezel and integrated H-link bracelet, the Marbella also includes nods to Genta’s other most famous designs, the Patek Philippe Nautilus and Audemars Piguet Royal Oak. Seiko’s 145th Anniversary Limited Edition “Edo purple” collection includes the affordable solar quartz version of the Prospex Speedtimer. The “Edo purple” dial features a radiant sunburst finish with black subdials and gold plating on the hands and applied indices. The fixed bezel features a purple segment on the black aluminum bezel insert, marked with a tachymeter scale. It comes on a stainless steel three-link bracelet with a folding clasp. Part of Seiko’s third series of 145th-anniversary releases, the Alpinist gets an “Edo purple” dial, named after the distinctive hue that represented Tokyo’s original formation. It otherwise retains all the same details from the collection’s 2025 revision, including an internal rotating compass bezel, “cyclops” date magnifier, gold accents and the stylized Alpinist logo that dates back to 1959. It is a limited edition of 7,000 pieces, slated for an October release. The Navy SEAL 3550 reimagines one of Luminox’s most iconic tactical watches with a slimmer, more ergonomic 44mm Carbonox case that’s no less formidable than those that came before it. A Swiss Ronda 515 quartz movement powers the watch, while 16 Luminox Light Technology tubes deliver constant, self-powered illumination for up to 25 years. Add a screw-down crown, anti-reflective sapphire crystal, unidirectional rotating bezel and 200m water resistance, and this is a serious tool watch for divers and military enthusiasts alike. Casio’s new MTP-E740 borrows the looks of Seiko’s Time Sonar. It won’t be an exact dupe of the ’70s icon, but you still get the same transparent dial (and in five colors) and bilingual day-date wheel. What’s more, these can be yours at around one-fourth of the price. Trafford Watch Co., founded in Austin in 2023, releases its first regular production lineup, the Core Collection. It includes the Touring GMT, one of the brand’s most popular one-off releases. The Core version features a fully lumed dial, lumed hands and lumed date wheel seen at 6:00. It is a “true” GMT, powered by the well-respected Miyota Caliber 9075 automatic movement, regulated in-house to +/- 10 seconds per day. Originally launched in 2018 as a reimagining of the brand’s 1980s military prototypes, Timex’s Mk1 Chronograph has become a fan favorite, thanks to its archival history and timeless styling. While these additions to the lineup retain the watch’s overall styling and functionality, including its reliable quartz movement, they get a big upgrade in the form of a sunray finish on the dials — a seemingly simple change that adds overall refinement. Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Selfwinding Flying Tourbillon ‘Bleu Nuit, Nuage 50’ Ceramic AP’s second try at making a Royal Oak in full ‘Bleu Nuit, Nuage 50’ ceramic, which is the same shade of blue as the most iconic Royal Oak dial, adds a flying tourbillon at 6:00 courtesy of the brand’s Calibre 2950 automatic movement. The “open-heart” version of Orient’s modern sports watch is having its last hurrah. The current lineup was introduced in 2024 and got a final limited-edition restock, according to the brand. It’s 41mm stainless steel case holds a small seconds dial with a round aperture exposing the balance wheel below, available in crimson, sky blue, green and pearly white with a gold-tone case and bracelet. G-Shock Mudmaster Master of Horizon Gold GG-B100XMH-5A G-Shock debuts its Master of Horizon Gold collection, highlighted by this stunning new Mudmaster. The rugged adventure watch complements its 200m of water resistance and extreme shock and mud resistance with a yellow gold ion-plated bezel inspired by the look of the horizon where the earth meets the sky. Not long after reviving the 1976 Lexington with a gold-tone case, which promptly sold out, Timex followed it up with a polished-steel variation. The two-hand, time-only dial features the same brushed metal plate with a black printed “Tank” track, but the hands are updated with a blue finish. It comes on a brown embossed alligator leather strap with a steel pin buckle. Timex throws back to the ’80s with its new Retroware Digital. This completely original watch isn’t a reissue but pays homage to old-school digital sports watches like the Ironman and Triathlon. It features a large, quirky time display that takes up most of the dial. Meanwhile, underneath sits a full calendar readout. The timepiece also has chronograph, timer and alarm functions as well, all backed by Indiglo for nighttime visibility. Seiko links up with Honda for this 5 Sports Field tribute to the 1980s Motocompo folding scooter. The watch features numerous nods to the bike, including the yellow dial color, Honda-branded horizontal bar, dot-style typeface and much more. This year marks the 50th anniversary of Shelby’s iconic Aluminum Edition Daytona Coupe. In honor of the monumental occasion, the legendary motorsports outfit has teamed up with one of the most storied American watchmaking brands to build the chromed-out Bulova Shelby Racer Chronograph. A more traditional alternative to the brand’s 150th edition Shelby Racer Chronograph, this one gets a high-polish stainless steel case (with a matching bracelet and a leather alternative strap), mirror-polished chronograph dial, a high-precision quartz movement and subtle co-branding. Breitling Professional Endurance Pro 44 Ironman World Championship 2026 Breitling continues its partnership with the Ironman triathlon with this limited-edition Endurance Pro chronograph featuring a titanium case, a SuperQuartz movement and a turquoise color scheme inspired by the Ironman Championship’s Hawaiian setting. Panerai gives the Luminor an advanced new build while retaining its classic look. The case, siganture crown lock and fixed bezel are made of the proprietary Carbotech, a carbon fiber and polymer compound that is 64 percent lighter than titanium and highly corrosion-resistant. It retains the black 3-6-9-12 sandwich dial with pencil hands and a small seconds at 9:00. It comes on a brown leather strap with contrast box stitching and a titanium pin buckle, along with a black rubber pin buckle strap. Seiko draws inspiration from Austria’s Lake Hallstatt for this limited-edition, European-exclusive dive watch. The resultant sunburst green dial with gold accents is reminiscent of Seiko’s iconic alpine-inspired watch, the Alpinist. Casio updates its affordable MRW dive watch series with the 240H. Compared to the outgoing model (230H), the new quartz timepiece makes subtle changes, swapping the day-date window with only a date display and changing the dial text from “WR 100M” to “WR 100BAR.” It’s available in three stealthy new resin colorways as well and still features its 60-minute graduated bezel. Unimatic X San Francisco Market Modello Uno U1-SFM The Italian watchmaker teamed up with the Korean retailer San Francisco Market to design a galvanic dial where no two examples are identical. An electrochemical process creates a glittering speckled arrangement over a radiant navy blue background, mimicking stars in a clear night sky. The time-only dive watch is powered by a Seiko Caliber NH35A automatic movement, and comes on a navy blue leather pin buckle strap, with a navy blue TPU pin buckle strap provided as well. It is a limited edition of 111 pieces. The Pro Trek PRJ-B001EX-1 is the most distinctive entry yet in Casio’s Hiker Line. Its reversible cloth strap flips into a soft-shell pouch, complete with a built-in pocket for a key, coins or folded cash. It also features a carabiner loop for clipping to a tent or pack. A rotary guard bezel locks the side buttons against accidental presses on the trail. Tough Solar charging and Bluetooth round out the package, housed in a 50.3 x 46mm biomass-resin case rated to 100 meters of water resistance.

item.title: The Best New Turntable Releases of 2026 (So Far)
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.65
Vinyl continues to lead the way when it comes to the resurgence of physical media, with record sales having increased every year since 2007. In fact, last year vinyl record sales surpassed $1 billion for the first time since 1983. Naturally, this has encouraged many of the biggest names in hi-fi to get back in (or ramp up) the turntable business. Today, brands like Pro-Ject, Sony, Audio-Technica, Technics and Teac all make a wide variety of turntables. Some are designed for entry-level vinyl enthusiasts. Some are designed for truly elite audiophiles with seriously deep pockets. For far in 2026, a lot of new turntables have been announced. Below, we’ve rounded up the most notable of these releases.

item.title: Timex Adds Subtle Camo To Its Classic Expedition Sierra Hiking Watch
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.61
About five years ago, Timex expanded its long-running Expedition lineup to fill a gap between the entry-level Scout and the newly introduced North Field Post on the premium side. The model was called the Expedition Sierra, and not only was it a solid mid-tier field watch but it was the watchmaker’s affordable response to the legendary Hamilton Khaki Field (it’s about a third the price of even the quartz version of the Hamilton timepiece). Now, Timex takes the Sierra’s military pretense to new heights with camo-dialed options that surprisingly don’t eschew the model’s versatility. Playing the field Landing in green and tan, the new Sierra colorways feature subtle monochromatic images of forest scenery in the backdrop. Fortunately, Timex doesn’t go with traditional camo here, still making these solid GADA watches if you’d like them to be.

item.title: 13 Cool New Gadgets to Keep on Your Radar
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.58
If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Another week down, and, per usual, a bunch of new tech and gadgets have been announced. This past week, Bose introduced new QuietComfort noise-canceling headphones, Marantz revealed an updated range of AV receivers, and Klipsch unveiled its latest loudspeaker range. But that’s just scratching the surface. Below, we’ve rounded up all the most interesting new releases and announcements you might have missed from the past week. Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) Bose’s second-generation QuietComfort Headphones bring several features previously exclusive to its pricier Ultra lineup down to a more accessible tier. They have improved sound and active noise-cancellation, and finally support lossless audio (up to 24-bit/48kHz) when using a wired connection. At $359, they are $90 cheaper than Bose’s flagship QuietComfort Ultra Headphones. Fiio’s Snowsky Echo Nano is a portable hi-fi player that, according to the brand, “reimagines the iconic 2000s era MP3 player.” It doesn’t run any apps, so you won’t find Spotify or Apple Music on it. Instead, it supports a microSD card (up to 256GB) and provides a distraction-free way of listening to your digital music library. It features a Cirrus Logic CS43131 DAC and can play high-resolution audio, with native DSD decoding alongside support for WAV, FLAC, APE, MP3, M4A and OGG formats. Klipsch has introduced the next generation of its top-of-the-line loudspeakers. The Reference Premiere III features acoustic and design advancements over its 2022 Reference Premiere II counterparts. There are nine passive loudspeakers in the brand-new Reference Premiere III range, which includes three floorstanding, two bookshelf, two center channel, and two surround sound speakers. The range goes on sale October 2026. The Cinema 50 Series 2 is a new-and-improved version of the 2022-released Cinema 50, and it’s the flagship model in the Cinema Series 2 range. It’s a 9.4-channel AV receiver that’s capable of delivering 110 watts per channel. And it features 8 HDMI inputs, each supporting 8K video. Compared to its predecessor, it features a new 32-bit, eight-channel DAC and has been integrated with the latest HEOS platform for superior multi-room functionality. The Cinema 60 Series 2 is the midrange option in Marantz’s new Cinema Series 2 range. It’s a 7.4-channel AV receiver that can deliver 100 watts per channel. It has a 8 HDMI inputs, but only three support 8K video. According to the brand, it “elevates everything you love about movies, all in a timeless, feature-rich design.” The Cinema 70s Series 2 is a 7.4-channel AV receiver that is capable of delivering 50 watts per channel. It has many of the same features as the Cinema 60 Series 2, but is half as powerful and roughly half the size. According to the brand, it’s designed to ensure “unforgettable home theater experiences even in smaller spaces.” The Astell&Kern PD5 is the successor to the A&norma SR35 and the company’s new entry-level portable hi-fi player. It packs an octa-core processor and runs on an Android-based operating system, giving you quick access to your favorite streaming services. It features an eight-DAC audio architecture (which is twice as many DACs as its predecessor) and supports bit-perfect playback up to 32-bit/384kHz PCM and native DSD256. The Q Acoustics 3040c is the newest addition to the brand’s entry-level 3000c range of loudspeakers. It’s positioned as the slightly smaller sibling to the 3050c, the range’s flagship floorstanding speaker. The 3040c features the same driver, cabinet, and acoustic innovations, and looks nearly identical, but it’s $100 cheaper and a better fit for smaller-to-medium-sized rooms. Triangle’s AIO Twin is an entry-level active speaker system that supports a wide range of wired and wireless connections. It has a switchable MM phono preamplifier, so you can connect the speakers directly to a turntable. The system can be used as TV or desktop speakers, too. And it supports Wi-Fi and Bluetooth streaming. The company has introduced the system in a new Macassar finish inspired by Macassar ebony, an Indonesian hardwood known for its dark brown color and striking golden-yellow stripes. Sony released its current flagship noise-canceling headphones, the WH-1000XM6, in May 2026. And they feature some key upgrades of their predecessors, the 2022-released XM5, including improved sound, call quality and active noise-cancellation, as well as a more foldable design. Since the release, Sony has rolled out a few new colorways of the XM6. And the latest one is Olive Gray. The DJI Mic Mini 2S is the latest addition to the brand’s Mic Mini lineup of wireless microphone and transmitter systems. Naturally, it works similarly to others, providing a reliable way for content creators to record on-the-go audio. However, the Mic Mini 2S is positioned as an upgraded version of the Mic Mini 2, which was just released in April 2026. It adds 32-bit floating-point internal recording, providing additional backup for your camera or smartphone recordings. Also, it can work with up to four transmitters (whereas the Mic Mini 2 supports only two). Sadly, like many of DJI’s latest releases, it’s unclear whether or when this will get a US release. The Creative XF1 is a set of powered computer speakers designed to deliver impressive sound from a small package. Each speaker has a bi-amp configuration, meaning a dedicated amp powers the tweeter and the woofer, and the system delivers 72 watts and has a frequency range of 55Hz to 40kHz. The system features USB-C and aux inputs, so they can easily be used as speakers for your computer or turntable. They have built-in Bluetooth with LDAC support, so you can stream high-resolution audio to them. And they are compatible with the Creative Nexus app, which allow you to further fine-tune audio settings. Nothing’s budget-friendly brand, CMF, has launched its first pair of open-ear wireless earbuds. The CMF Clip Pro are earbuds with a clip-on design, popularized by Bose’s Open Ultra Earbuds, that grip the outside of your ears sort of like earrings. They are designed to play music while also letting ambient sounds in, so they’re safer to wear when running, biking or exercising in public. One of their standout features is the charging case’s smart dial, which lets you adjust volume and control playback without touching the earbuds or your smartphone. Available in three colors: Dark Grey, Light Grey and Coral. About the Author: Tucker Bowe has been on Gear Patrol’s editorial team since 2014. With a passion for consumer tech and hi-fi, he tracks everything from headphones and turntables to smartphones and wearables. If it lights up or makes noise, he probably covers it. item.title: Victrola’s Soundstage Turns an Entry-Level Turntable Into a Compact Vinyl Hi-Fi System
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.57
Victrola is well known for its budget-friendly turntables, many of which are actually all-in-one turntables that have built-in speakers. While this makes listening to vinyl super easy, it’s generally frowned upon by hi-fi enthusiasts because, well, it doesn’t sound great. But over the last year or so, Victrola has gotten into more serious hi-fi systems. Its range of Stream turntables, which are among the few Sonos-compatible turntables on the market, don’t have a built-in speaker and can cost between $800 to $1,500 depending on the model. And now, the company has released a specialty speaker that’s specifically designed and engineered to sit underneath your turntable. This way, it creates a vinyl hi-fi system that doesn’t take up much space. Victrola Soundstage The Soundstage is kind of like of soundbase for your turntable. It has a matching footprint, so it doesn’t take up more space. And it is a special vibration-isolated cabinet, so when playing, it does not shake and disrupt the turntable’s playback. For those in the know, this category of “turntable soundbase” has been well established by Andover Audio, which also makes some really high-end all-in-one turntables.

item.title: Nike Is Selling Almost Every Running Shoe It Makes Way Under Retail Right Now
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.56
Marathon builds never quite go exactly according to plan. But one thing is certain. Whether you’re training for your first 26.2, consider yourself a seasoned sub-elite or simply dream of one day crossing the Staten Island bridge by foot, the miles won’t run themselves. Now Nike won’t make it any easier, as much as the brand will try to convince you otherwise. But it can make it somewhat cheaper to lace up in shoes designed to go the distance. That’s because Nike’s vast back-to-school sale is chock-full of deep discounts on nearly every running shoe it makes. Notably, the styles extend beyond the end-of-cycle styles that typically make up deal fare. Included are the newest generation of the reliable Pegasus, the fan-favorite Vomero Plus and even the ACG Ultrafly, Nike’s pinnacle race shoe leading the All Conditions Gear relaunch. Browse the highlights below or head over to Nike’s official website to shop the broader sale. Nike Pegasus Premium Men’s Road Running Shoes -
$230 (32% off)

item.title: Timex Streamlines Its Crowd-Pleasing, Affordable Weekender Watch
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.50
One of the best things about Timex is its catalogs relative affordability. For generations, this brand has made timeless, stylish, dependable wristwatches accessible even to those on an extremely tight budget. Since its introduction in 2011, the Timex Weekender has been a quintessential example of that particular blend of factors. And now, it gets a pair of new editions in the Timex Weekender New England series, including a classic time-only option and a chronograph. Working for the Weekender This new series consists of a pair of watches. The first of them is a classic time-only offering called simply the Timex Weekender New England. This is actually a rerelease of an existing watch, boasting some fairly significant tweaks. Yet it retains its original spirit. The biggest alteration is to its case size. The new version measures just 34 millimeters in diameter, whereas the original was 39 millimeters. That makes this one positively petite, by comparison. It’s also more wearable and a touch more refined.

item.title: Christopher Ward’s New Affordable Dive Watch Borrows a Page from Omega
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.42
Years before the days of the Bel Canto, the Twelve and the Loco, Christopher Ward was known mainly for its Trident dive watch. Notably, the brand’s flagship, with its wave-textured dial, was frequently cited as an affordable alternative to the iconic Omega Seamaster Diver 300M. CW’s homage days are largely left in its past, but not entirely. The watches in the brand’s diverse and popular Sealander family bear strong resemblance to Rolex’s Explorer II and Oyster Perpetual, and even the Twelve draws a lot of comparisons to the far more expensive Czapek Antarctique. (The two watches actually share a designer, so it’s understandable.) The Trident, meanwhile, largely stands on its own four lugs these days as an original (and very attractive) design. But a new limited edition feels more like the CW of old, with a design trait borrowed from its old pal, Omega. The new Trident 30×30 was made in collaboration with the Blue Marine Foundation and is named after the organization’s 30×30 Ocean Action Plan, which seeks to protect 30 percent of the planet’s water by 2030. The watch is part of the Trident Reef family and thus features a colorful aluminum bezel insert color-matched to unique aluminum sides on its 41mm steel “sandwich” case. Here, the color used for these aluminum bits is teal, which is also used for the Aquaflex rubber strap and dial.

item.title: Volkswagen’s ID. Buzz Just Unlocked Some New Adventure Van Potential
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.42
Although Volkswagen didn’t design the ID. Buzz as an overlander from the factory, the aftermarket has been eager to reinvent the platform. After all, from lifts to full-on camper conversions, the electric van has already inspired a host of upgrades for excursions beyond the pavement. The right kit can give it a lot of promise. The latest of such options comes from a German off-road specialist named Seikel, as surfaced by Inside EVs. It’s far from a comprehensive overhaul, but it nevertheless provides the ID. Buzz with much-improved adventure potential. A light off-road redux If you’re not already familiar with Seikel, the company is well-steeped with off-road and VW expertise. It first set up shop in 1949, and it’s been dabbling with Volkswagen vans since the ‘80s.

item.title: You May Not Like It, but the Mazda MX-5 Miata’s Fate Is Inevitably Electric
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 4.13
Welp, it appears the Mazda MX-5 Miata’s electrified fate is sealed. New reports recently surfaced, citing conversations with key executives who essentially confirmed that the next-gen Miata will become an EV to some degree. Germany’s Auto Motor und Sport recently chatted with Mazda’s CEO, Masahiro Moro. In their chat, Moro basically said both Mazda and the world need to be prepared for a Miata not powered by internal combustion. The next-gen Miata MX-5 is going electric in some capacity Over the past several months, rumors have ramped up regarding the next-generation Miata. That’s because the current model’s been with us for about a decade, meaning it is very much due for a replacement. Mazda generally treats the world to a new generation every 10 years. But because of a variety of factors (such as pumping the brakes on its electrification strategy and trying to weather the current geopolitical and economic circumstances), the company has had to delay the next-gen MX-5.

item.title: Suzuki’s Approachable New Gixxer Embraces the Iconic Bike’s Four-Decade Legacy
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.99
Affectionately known as the Gixxer, Suzuki’s GSX-R nameplate is one of the brand’s most recognizable and long-running franchises. Dating back to the mid-1980s, the bike was nonetheless on death’s door until last month, when the brand announced the 40th anniversary editions of the GSX-R1000 models. Now comes news that the brand is doing the same with one of the most approachable Gixxers, the GSX-R600, as well as the GSX-R750. The anniversary edition of the former is one of three new treatments, all temptingly priced under $13,000. This is 40ish It’s a bit odd to see Suzuki lean into the 40th anniversary branding now, as the original GSX-R750F dates back to 1985, but it is legendary enough that we won’t split hairs. In reality, we’re just glad to see the nameplate back from the dead, as until recently, it had not had a meaningful update since 2022 and had been widely discontinued around the world (but not the US) in 2024.

item.title: Converse Slaps Vintage Suede on Its Underrated ‘90s-Inspired Sneaker
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.91
Perennially living in the shadow of the Chuck Taylor and Jack Purcell, the Converse One Star is still an iconic sneaker, albeit with a somewhat strange history. The silhouette debuted in 1974 as a suede basketball shoe, but went dormant for a while before coming back hard in the ’90s thanks in part to pro skaters who gravitated toward its flat sole and low profile. That skating connection gave the shoe a slightly different cultural lineage than the Chuck Taylor’s art-school associations or the Purcell’s court heritage. Now, Converse is leaning into the One Star’s retro heritage, dropping two colorways that look like they came straight out of the ‘90s. Aged to perfection Leaning into the silhouette’s understated character, the new variants come in black and burgundy uppers. Converse describes the material as aged suede, which gives the sneakers a broken-in quality from the start. This is long-pile suede with a slightly faded look.

item.title: 7 Cool New Motorcycles You Might’ve Missed from BSA, Indian, Yamaha and More
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.88
If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more As much as the moto industry continuously rolls forward, it’s hugely aware of its past, too, as this week’s trio of retro-leaning releases reminds us. Finally headed our way, Yamaha’s coolest modern triple recalls racing’s golden ’80s and ’90s), BSA’s charming small-bore roadster picks up a hue referencing the nameplate’s inaugural 1948 edition and Indian’s latest cruiser pays tribute to monumental 1938 gathering. Get the scoop on those thrilling throwbacks (and plenty of forward-looking motos too) below. Indian Chief Vintage Sturgis, SD Edition Paying tribute to the original Indian riders who gathered to race around Sturgis way back in 1938, this limited-edition bike boasts a classic two-tone red-and-cream paint scheme, headdress logo and painted number recalling bikes of that era. Other throwback elements include the illuminated warbonnet, skirted fenders, wire-spoke wheels, brown solo seat and vintage bars. Yet under the hood it packs plenty of modern power and tech, including the brand’s air-cooled Thunderstroke 116 V-Twin engine producing 120 ft-lbs. of torque, three ride modes and a 4-inch round touchscreen display for accessing navigation, weather, bike data and more. Now boasting a Doctor Doom skin, this bike punches above its displacement in the crowded Indian commuter segment. Paired to a five-speed gearbox, its 124.8cc three-valve single produces an affable 11.22 horsepower and 8.7 ft-lbs of torque. Top variants add a TFT display, iGO riding modes with Boost, single-channel ABS and a 5-step adjustable mono-shock. As a tribute to great American racer Kenny Roberts, Yamaha added a new ‘Legend Yellow’ option to its 2026 XSR900 GP catalog. Bearing the iconic speed block livery, the color scheme transforms the GP from a mere lookalike into a true period-correct imitator. Even better, the bike is back in the news this week thanks to California Air Resources Board paperwork indicating it is finally coming to the United States, likely later this year. BSA’s revived 350 returns to the headlines thanks to its new Mist Green colorway, which pays tribute to the original 1948 Bantam. It’s a modern bike nonetheless, boasting a 334cc liquid-cooled DOHC single producing 29 horsepower and 22 ft-lbs of torque through a 6-speed gearbox. Dual-channel ABS, telescopic forks and twin adjustable rear shocks underpin the chassis, while a round headlight, teardrop tank and digital dash balance retro style with modern utility. This sci-fi-inspired electric café racer is built around what Real Motors calls an Electric Analogue philosophy: modern EV power delivered with an old-school, analog riding feel. It boasts a PMSM Drive making 100 horsepower and a pretty bonkers 738 ft-lbs of torque at the rear wheel, plus on-board level 2 charging, premium suspension and a small screen that appears to deliver critical info about the bike but not too much else, as intended. This Ninja pairs a 636cc liquid-cooled inline-four engine with a pressed-aluminum perimeter frame, a combination that delivers strong low- and mid-range torque without sacrificing top-end push. Tech-wise, it’s loadedwith KQS quick-shift, three-mode KTRC traction control, KIBS anti-lock brakes, a 4.3-inch TFT display. Pirelli Diablo Rosso IV tires and dual 310mm radial-mount calipers round out the compelling package. The Leten LT190 is an underbone-style adventure moto that punches well above its class. Its liquid-cooled 188cc single comes with DLC coating and a CVT. Standard tech includes switchable ABS, traction control, heated grips and even keyless ignition. Along with some hand guards and a high-mount front fender, it rocks a slick rear pillion that doubles as a luggage rack and backrest. Now managing editor, Steve has served in a variety of roles with GP since 2019. Having previously written and edited for such publications as Men’s Health, Men’s Journal, Esquire and ESPN, he enjoys covering a range of topics — but mostly those pertaining to cycling, snow sports, pocket knives and motos — and dreams of a utopian world in which everyone’s bike seat is at the proper height. item.title: Hoka’s Classic Retro Runner Gets an Earthy, Japanese-Inspired Update
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.84
Hoka has never been particularly shy about color, often opting for vibrant hues that underscore its maximalist approach to running shoes. So you’d be forgiven for not immediately clocking the brand’s latest release as an old-school classic. The upcoming Bondi 7 Beams revisits an older generation of the brand’s go-to max-cushioned trainer, reimagining it through Beams’s minimalist lens. Here, that means two new colorways “reminiscent of carefully composed rock gardens and weathered temple timbers,” the brands say.

item.title: Teva’s New Trailpeak Is Its Most Lightweight Trail Runner to Date
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.67
Before the likes of Keen came about in the early ‘00s, Teva was long synonymous with outdoor sandals. And for many, it still is. Redefining the idea of what a sandal can do, the California-based company changed the game with the debut of its Hurricane in 1984. It wasn’t the first sandal designed for the outdoors but it was able to balance ruggedness, protection and weight, really for the first time. For years, Teva exclusively made sandals. From adventure-focused models, it transitioned to running sandals. Then in 2001, the brand came out with its first closed-toe shoes, the Wraptor and Elden. Over the years, Teva’s had plenty of impressive trail runners, from the X1 Racer to the experimental TevaSphere line. But recently, Teva aims to reclaim its athletic heritage by engineering top-tier trail running gear once again by launching the Teva Bureau of Adventure (TBA). This athlete-driven program features ultrarunners like Mike Wardian and Erin Ton who prototype and test high-performance trail shoes and hybrid running sandals. The latest from the TBA is the brand-new Trailpeak, a featherweight trail runner that Teva calls its “cannonball into the deep end” of the category.

item.title: Yes, Volkswagen is Genuinely Taking Aim at the Toyota Tacoma and Ford Ranger
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.48
Volkswagen is apparently now serious about building a new midsize pickup for Americans. Multiple reports from Handelsblatt and Reuters indicate Wolfsburg’s newfound interest in entering the segment after it has seen a monumental uptick in demand. According to the report, which cites an unnamed source close to the matter, VW wants to build a competitor to fight the Toyota Tacoma, Ford Ranger, Chevrolet Colorado and other midsize trucks. The decision supposedly comes after Americans have demonstrated keen interest in more affordable, smaller pickups over typical full-sized ones. Finally, an actual Volkswagen pickup meant for us When shopping for any type of utilitarian vehicle with an open bed, Volkswagen isn’t typically the first brand to come to mind. At least here in America, it isn’t. That’s because Volkswagen never sold a conventional pickup in the States. The story is quite different elsewhere, where VW sells the Amarok, a model originally introduced in 2010.

item.title: Mitsubishi’s Potentially Brewing a Pajero-Based Toyota RAV4 Rival
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.38
Mitsubishi isn’t confining its new Pajero revival to the standard full-size model. The Japanese automaker is apparently also brewing up a smaller variant to take on the likes of the Toyota RAV4 and crew. Moreover, the Pajero’s lineup expansion apparently won’t stop there. The model’s product planners are also supposedly working on a tiny Kei car variant in a bid to compete with rigs like the Suzuki Jimny. The Pajero wants to also fight the Toyota RAV4 and co. Mitsubishi’s revival of the Pajero most certainly has us excited, as it’s one of the Toyota Land Cruiser’s arch-rivals. But according to multiple reports and the latest development, the full-size model won’t be the only offering. The Japanese automaker is also keeping with tradition by offering multiple variants. One of those will apparently be a smaller version to battle the Toyota RAV4 and its associated competition. And another will also surface to likely compete against the Suzuki Jimny and its competitors. However, the latter probably won’t make to American shores if the Pajero returns as the Montero.

item.title: Nike ACG Already Teased Its Next Big Trail Shoe
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.36
The dust has yet to fully settle from Nike’s relaunch of ACG, led by the release of the Ultrafly, Radical Airflow and Zegama Hike. But the world already knows its next big launch. The brand recently took to social media to tease a brand-new ACG shoe called the ACG Kigerfly, the prototype of which has already put up impressive times on the trail-racing circuit. While specifics remain sparse for now, the images do reveal a few key details about the upcoming silhouette. The Kigerfly shows a sleek, low-profile build that leans more toward trail-influenced running than ACG’s chunkier hiking-boot lineage.

item.title: Timex’s New Affordable Sports Watch Is a Dead Ringer for an IWC Icon
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.31
From divers that look like Omega Seamasters to chronographs that ape the Zenith El Primero‘s tricolor layout to myriad Rolex clones, Timex has its finger on the pulse of watch culture when it comes to design. The brand’s latest runs a bit more obscure than Rolex or Omega, but still lands firmly in icon territory, as its new addition to the affordable Q lineup of sports watches looks like a close cousin of the Gérald Genta-designed IWC Ingenieur. Timex’s new watch is the Q Timex Marbella. It’s a 40.5mm integrated sports watch in full stainless steel with lumed hands and applied indices, 50m water resistance and a quartz movement. But the real story is the design. The watch’s case is topped with a round, circular brushed bezel with polished sides secured with exposed bolts, and the case is integrated into an H-link case.

item.title: Telo’s Tiny Pickup Truck Just Upped the Ante Against Ford and Slate
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.28
Between Ford’s Fathom name reveal and Slate’s new starter pack customization options, the affordable electric pickup space is getting more charged by the day. Eager to stay in the conversation, California-based startup Telo also recently gave an update on the progress of its challenger in the MT1. It’s a noteworthy one, too, since it makes for some big gains in compact utility. As such, even though Telo’s truck is shaping up to be a bit different from the pickups Ford and Slate have planned, I’d still argue it just upped the ante against both vehicles. Telo’s MT1 tows big That’s because, according to the company’s latest YouTube video, the MT1 can haul even more than initially promised. Telo is now saying that its dual-motor truck is now good for a whopping 8,000 pounds, and even the single-motor is good for a 6,600-pound rating.

item.title: Carhartt’s Fall-Ready Layer Softens Its Rugged DNA Without Sacrificing Utility
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 3.15
Carhartt may be synonymous with rugged capability, but the brand also produces a variety of softer, still-capable hoodies, T-shirts, beanies and more. Its latest hybrid outerwear combines the brand’s heritage workwear influence with a modern build and materials, resulting in a functional jacket that’s as soft as it is capable. The Paxton Quilted Shirt Jac combines 10.2-ounce quilted fleece with a loose fit, offering warmth and easy layering. A snap-front closure makes it easy to put on and take off, while the shirt-jac silhouette gives it a versatile look that works well beyond the job site. Designed for everything from workdays to weekend DIY projects, the Paxton looks soft and comfortable but offers utility in both obvious and less-visible ways. That utility comes in the form of multiple pockets for keeping essentials close at hand, along with the brand’s proprietary Rain Defender water-repellent technology, which helps moisture bead and roll off the fleece fabric. While this is a women’s-specific style, the size range extends from XS to 3XL, giving a wide variety of body sizes and shapes the opportunity to find a comfortable fit in this versatile shacket.

item.title: Volkswagen’s Most Iconic Camper Van Raises the Bar Yet Again
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.98
Volkswagen has done it again with its iconic California camper van. The Wolfsburg’s commercial division, or the department in charge of all of its camper vans, just revealed a huge first for both the brand and its iconic line of California camper vans. Say hello to the world’s first-ever, all-electric Volkswagen ID. California. This marks VW’s first attempt at emissions-free glamping. The company also revealed some new, innovative features, thanks to the model’s increase level of interior space. The California finally goes electric Since it was based on the 1980s T3 Transporter, the California has always served as VW’s iconic multi-purpose vehicle. That means it has depended on a wide range of internal combustion engines, from gutless, clattery and smelly diesels to peppy VR6s and turbo-fours. Now, EV and environmental van fans can enjoy the iconic VW glamping lifestyle, all without having to fill up a petrol or diesel tank. As such, the new ID. California is unsurprisingly based on the ID. Buzz’s all-electric platform.

item.title: This Audiophile Amplifier Is Goldmund’s “Most Ambitious” Hi-Fi Product Ever
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.81
Goldmund is a Swiss luxury audio manufacturer that is well regarded in elite hi-fi circles for its extremely high-end audio components and loudspeakers. Many of which cost more than most homes. For context, the company’s current flagship active loudspeakers, the Gaïa Active, cost roughly $600,000. Its newest passive loudspeakers, the Rhea Passive and Theia Passive, go for around $108,000/pair and $215,000/pair, respectively. And, most recently, Goldmund introduced a stereo integrated amplifier, the Telos 670, which goes for around $30,000. A fairly entry-level hi-fi component by the brand’s standards. Now, however, the company is skyrocketing back up to hi-fi stratosphere with its newest flagship amplifier, the Telos 9800. It’s calling it “one of [its] most ambitious specialist hi-fi products” ever. Goldmund’s flagship power amp The Telos 9800 is the most high-end, high-power amplifier that Goldmund has ever created.

item.title: New West KnifeWorks Upgraded Its MagnaCut EDC Knife with a Precision Button Lock
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.58
In October of last year, my colleague, Steve Mazzucchi, wrote about a stunning MagnaCut EDC knife from a surprising brand. That knife was the New West KnifeWorks Glory Folder. While the original was pretty damn great, it wasn’t perfect. That said, it didn’t need a full redesign, either. Thankfully, the NWKW Glory Folder 2.0 delivers tweaks that fix precisely what needs fixing and leaves everything else intact. Newfound glory The starting point for the Glory Folder 2.0 was already incredibly solid. Honestly, it could take the cake as NWKW’s best knife to date. At the very least, it’s an exceptionally compelling entry into the EDC world. For the most part, this new version doesn’t change much. The overall size (7.125 inches) and the silhouette remain unchanged. The materials also remain.

item.title: Nissan’s Next Most Important Model Will Really Get Toyota RAV4 and Honda CR-V Fans’ Attention
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.56
Toyota RAV4 and Honda CR-V fans will soon have a serious contender to consider from Nissan. The next-gen Rogue Sport’s global variant, the Qashqai, just broke a Guinness World Record for traveling over 1,000 miles without ever refueling. And it was all achieved thanks to the Qashqai’s unique propulsion system. It’s neither entirely gas nor entirely electric, and it’s not quite a conventional hybrid. It’s on track to be an absolute game-changer. A segment’s first extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) The vehicle in question is the Nissan Qashqai e-Power. If that name sounds distantly familiar, that’s because the Qashqai is basically America’s old Rogue Sport. Or formerly, the second-generation Rogue. It’s just named the Qashqai in the Japanese Domestic Market and European and Asian export markets. Nissan discontinued the Rogue Sport for the States after it spawned off a larger Rogue model based on the global X-Trail.

item.title: The 19 Best Buck Knives of 2026 (So Far)
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.56
If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Technically speaking, Buck Knives didn’t begin commercially operating until 1947. However, its history dates back much further, to 1902, when budding blacksmith Hoyt Buck sought a new, better way to temper steel. While there’s a lot of history between then and now, the brand has marched through it all, remaining one of the most significant knifemaking brands in American history. To this day, Buck is leading the charge, proving how prolific and innovative it remains, even when tweaking classics like its Slim Heritage Elite lineup and a recent patriotic spin on the Bowie knife. Check out all the best blades the brand has come out with this year so far below. That’s no moon…it’s Buck’s latest Buck of the Month launch. And for May, the brand has put out a properly sharp tribute to a galaxy far, far away with this Rebel-colored EDC blade. Of course, the “Galaxy-worn” Stormtrooper white blade and orange handle are much more than just lookers; they’re also high-quality and performance-focused. For instance, the blade is Cerakote-finished MagnaCut steel, making it an incredible all-around performer from its edge retention down to its corrosion resistance. And the aluminum handle is both durable and lightweight. Put plainly, this is much more than just a cheeky gimmick. Buck is no stranger to modern EDC, despite being largely known for heritage knives and tools. For proof, take a gander at the 700 Nomad with its D2 steel blade, popular crossbar lock and textured aluminum handle. And it doesn’t stop there; the knife is also ambidextrous, courtesy of a reversible pocket clip and thumb stud deployment, too. And it’s available in a trio of distinct colorways. While the brand is best known for its heritage knives, Buck has still been keeping up with modern EDC styles, as well. The 698 Ferrox is a perfect example of how, combining workhorse D2 steel with a textured aluminum handle and a popular crossbar lock. Available in three colors, the knife also has a lanyard attachment point on the tail, an ambidextrous thumbstud deployment and a reversible pocket clip.

item.title: One of Porsche’s Rarest 911s Ever Unearthed Just Sold for as Much as a Mansion
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.52
There’s so much history surrounding the Porsche 911 that, even today, some very rare models are still coming out of the woodwork to much amazement. Enter one of RM Sotheby’s most recent auctions: one of just two 1993 964-based 911 Carrera RSR 3.8 ‘Strassenversions.’ The extraordinarily unique model recently crossed the block at the world-renowned auction house. As expected, it went for an ungodly sum of money, just over $4.7 million. While its sale price is very shocking, the story behind this specific example is even more incredible. Built to be driven, but never was As the story goes, Porsche built this specific 911 Carrera RSR 3.8 for a very special “Porsche VIP.” Being an “RSR,” which stands for “RennSport Rennwagen,” or “racing sport racing car” when translated to English from German, the RSR designates Porsche’s factory-built cup racecars. It’s the same lineage that today’s 992.1-based 911 RSR follows. They’re basically purpose-built racecars for the ultra-rich who compete in amateur and semi-professional motorsports as one of their delectable hobbies.

item.title: The Best New Böker Knives and Multi-Tools of 2026 (So Far)
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.49
Operating out of the historic German knife capital of Solingen, Böker has been dropping an incredibly wide variety of top-notch knives (and multi-tools) with great regularity from the start of the year till now. Two quick examples: the pricey M4 Sherman Damast Rose Gold draws inspiration and actual materials from an iconic WWII tank, while the much more affordable Modern Stockman updates a classic folding silhouette with fresh steel and style. In other words, whether you’re shopping for an all-business folder, a collector’s dream or something in between, you’ll find it among the dozens of excellent options below.

item.title: 6 New Pocket Knives You Might Have Missed from Böker, Civivi and More
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.47
If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Everyday carry can consume your attention: the weight of a knife in your pocket, the smoothness of a ball-bearing pivot, the way a blade holds its edge after weeks of use. This week, our coverage leaned into that obsession, with a run of folding knives that reward the kind of close inspection most people reserve for far more expensive purchases. Catch up on all the latest and greatest sharp-edged releases below. GiantMouse Jutland Slipjoint Blackout A limited run of 100 individually numbered pieces, this new interpretation takes GiantMouse’s award-winning Jutland Slipjoint (a two-time Field & Stream Best Hunting Folder honoree) and wraps it in an all-black PVD finish. The 2.65-inch S90V blade pairs with milled titanium scales and a traditional nail-nick opener in a non-locking format that travels well and cuts cleaner than its understated profile suggests. It’s a collector’s piece built for EDC devotees who want history in their pocket but demand modern performance. French knife designer and blacksmith Gabriel Berthelemy of La Forge Agab brings his signature aesthetic to this tactically oriented 2.43-ounce EDC folder. Its 2.64-inch Nitro-V harpoon blade carries a black oxide coating that fights scratches and kills unwanted glare. A ball-bearing pivot and front flipper deliver smooth one-handed deployment, while a liner lock, Coyote Tan G10 handle scales and a tip-up deep-carry clip round out the package. Kansept’s first collaboration with French designer Cédric Destombes combines a sleek silhouette with desirable materials. The 3.31-inch drop-point blade comes in Damascus steel or Elmax, depending on the variant, while the ergonomic handles boast a range of snazzy scales including 80S Camo Carbon Fiber and Rag Burl Current Micarta. Deployed via an ambidextrous thumb stud, the blade stays steady thanks to a reliable liner lock, while a sturdy tip-up clip, uniquely curved to match the handle’s contoured shape, makes it easy to tote in your pocket. Limited to 100 pieces worldwide and handcrafted in Boker’s Solingen factory, the Sherman EDC II Full-Ti is a collector-grade folder built for serious daily carry. Its 2.95-inch MagnaCut clip-point blade delivers elite edge retention, toughness and corrosion resistance. A full titanium handle with a unique rocky texture, a titanium frame lock and a pivot screw inspired by the M4 Sherman tank’s drive sprocket give this knife a distinct identity that sets it apart from anything else in the pocket. Civivi’s most popular knife of all time is its Elementum. But this version, handled by its big sister brand We Knife, gives the enduring silhouette its most significant upgrade ever. While the most common Elementums come with D2 tool steel, this one gets upgraded to MagnaCut super steel. Furthermore, it gets a topographical-engraved titanium handle, complete with a frame lock. It’s offered in two colorways: gray or all-black. Now managing editor, Steve has served in a variety of roles with GP since 2019. Having previously written and edited for such publications as Men’s Health, Men’s Journal, Esquire and ESPN, he enjoys covering a range of topics — but mostly those pertaining to cycling, snow sports, pocket knives and motos — and dreams of a utopian world in which everyone’s bike seat is at the proper height.

item.title: The Best Nike ACG Releases of 2026 (So Far)
item.description:
Source: Gear Patrol Score: 2.46
Nike’s bread and butter remains lightning-fast road runners and all manner of basketball shoes. But the company deserves some credit as one of the original performance-focused outdoor brands. ACG, short for All Conditions Gear, dates back to the 1980s, when Nike debuted silhouettes like the Lava Dome, Magma and Approach built specifically for hiking rough and rocky terrain. Though subsequent decades saw the respected sub-label devolve into lifestyle-driven designs coinciding with the rise of GORP, ACG relaunched in earnest earlier this year with a renewed focus on performance and innovation in the great outdoors. Catch up on some of the big releases headlining the label’s return to trails and mountains and stay tuned for more in the coming months. Nike is already teasing more high-profile drops, such as the Western States-winning Kigerfly.
